title: Beliefs & Foundations
description: General User → Beginner. A mix of familiar facts, broader basics and short everyday applications. Every question belongs to the Beginner level.
levelMethod: Beginner describes the knowledge required across all question styles. Styles are not difficulty levels. Editorial classification, not calibrated with learner response data.

review.referenceCheck: Primary-text references checked during preparation; this is not independent scholarly approval.

selectionHints.unknownResponse: Use I am not sure as a separate UI action, not a fifth option.

questions.question: How many gods do Muslims worship?
questions.explanation: Muslims worship Allah alone.

questions.question: Who created the heavens and the earth?
questions.explanation: Allah is the Creator of the heavens and the earth.

questions.question: Who is the final prophet in Islam?
questions.explanation: Muhammad (peace be upon him) is Allah's Messenger and the last of the prophets.

questions.question: Which book was revealed to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)?
questions.explanation: The Quran was revealed to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him).

questions.question: Which angel brought the Quran to the Prophet?
questions.explanation: Jibril brought the revelation by Allah's permission.

questions.question: What is the declaration of faith called?
questions.explanation: The Shahadah testifies to worshipping Allah alone and Muhammad being His Messenger.

questions.question: How many pillars of Islam are there?
questions.explanation: The well-known narration describes Islam as built on five pillars.

questions.question: Which word means the prescribed Islamic prayer?
questions.explanation: Salah is the prescribed prayer and one of Islam's pillars.

questions.question: Which pillar involves giving obligatory charity?
questions.explanation: Zakat is obligatory charity, subject to its conditions.

questions.question: In which month do Muslims observe the obligatory annual fast?
questions.explanation: Ramadan is the month of obligatory fasting for those required to fast.

questions.question: Hajj is a pilgrimage to the Sacred House in which city?
questions.explanation: The Sacred House, the Kabah, is in Makkah.

questions.question: Which of these is part of Islamic belief?
questions.explanation: Belief in Allah's angels is part of faith.

questions.question: What does belief in the Hereafter include?
questions.explanation: Muslims believe in resurrection and life after death.

questions.question: What is Jannah?
questions.explanation: Jannah is Paradise, promised by Allah to the believers who do good.

questions.question: What is Jahannam?
questions.explanation: Jahannam is Hell, a place of punishment in the Hereafter.

questions.question: What is dua?
questions.explanation: Dua means calling upon Allah and asking Him.

questions.question: What does tawbah mean?
questions.explanation: Tawbah means turning back to Allah in repentance.

questions.question: What does Tawhid mean?

options.text: Believing in Allah's oneness and worshipping Him alone
Believing that creation has no Creator

questions.explanation: Tawhid is the foundation of worshipping Allah alone.

questions.question: What is shirk?
questions.explanation: Shirk means giving a partner a share in what belongs to Allah alone.

questions.question: Does Allah know what is hidden in our hearts?

options.text: Only if we say it aloud

questions.explanation: Allah knows what people conceal as well as what they reveal.

questions.question: Can Allah hear a quiet dua?

options.text: Only when someone else repeats it
Only if it is shouted first

questions.explanation: Allah is All-Hearing; quietness does not prevent Him from hearing.

questions.question: Does Allah need food or drink?

options.text: No, He is free of need.

questions.explanation: Allah is self-sufficient and free of need.

questions.question: How should Muslims regard Allah's prophets?

options.text: Respect only the prophets from their own nation
Believe in and respect them all
Choose one prophet and reject every other prophet

questions.explanation: Belief in Allah's messengers includes accepting them, without rejecting some as messengers.

questions.question: Who is Isa (Jesus) in Islam?

options.text: A prophet and messenger of Allah

questions.explanation: The Quran identifies Isa as a messenger of Allah.

questions.question: Which prophet was taught the names by Allah?
questions.explanation: The Quran tells of Allah teaching Adam the names.

questions.question: Which prophet is also known in English as Abraham?
questions.explanation: Ibrahim is the Arabic name of the prophet known in English as Abraham.

questions.question: Which prophet is also known in English as Moses?
questions.explanation: Musa is the Arabic name of the prophet known in English as Moses.

questions.question: What is a main purpose of the Quran?

options.text: To replace every kind of learning

questions.explanation: The Quran describes itself as guidance.

questions.question: For what purpose did Allah create humans and jinn?
questions.explanation: The Quran connects the creation of humans and jinn with worshipping Allah.

questions.question: After doing wrong, what should a person do?
questions.explanation: Allah calls people not to despair of His mercy and to return to Him.

questions.question: How many beliefs are listed in the well-known explanation of iman?
questions.explanation: They include Allah, angels, books, messengers, the Last Day and divine decree.

questions.question: Belief in qadar means belief in what?

options.text: The idea that actions never matter

questions.explanation: Qadar concerns Allah's divine decree, including good and bad.

questions.question: The Tawrah is especially associated with which prophet?
questions.explanation: The Quran describes the Torah and the revelation given to Musa.

questions.question: Which prophet was given the Zabur?
questions.explanation: The Quran names Dawud as the prophet given the Zabur.

questions.question: Which prophet was given the Injil?
questions.explanation: The Quran states that Isa was given the Injil.

questions.question: Was Iblis an angel or one of the jinn?
questions.explanation: The Quran explicitly identifies Iblis as one of the jinn.

questions.question: How does the Quran describe the angels mentioned as carrying out Allah's commands?

options.text: They need people to worship them.
They decide who should be worshipped.

questions.explanation: The Quran describes these angels as obedient to Allah.

questions.question: What does Islam teach about our words and actions?

options.text: They are recorded and we are accountable.
Hidden actions can never be known.

questions.explanation: The Quran describes recording angels and the recording of speech.

questions.question: What does resurrection mean?

options.text: Being born as a different animal

questions.explanation: Allah will raise the dead for the Hereafter.

questions.question: Who knows the exact time of the Hour?
questions.explanation: The Quran places knowledge of its timing with Allah.

questions.question: You receive good news. Which phrase expresses gratitude to Allah?
questions.explanation: Alhamdulillah means that praise belongs to Allah.

questions.question: You are worried and want to make dua. Whom do you call upon?
questions.explanation: Dua is calling upon Allah, who hears His servants.

questions.question: You make dua quietly in your room. Can Allah hear you?

options.text: Only if the door is open

questions.explanation: Allah hears a quiet dua as well as an audible one.

questions.question: You have done something wrong. What should you ask Allah for?

options.text: A way to blame someone else

questions.explanation: Turn back to Allah and seek His forgiveness.

questions.question: No one sees you return a lost wallet. Does Allah know?

options.text: Only if the owner thanks you
Only if you tell a friend

questions.explanation: Allah knows our actions, including what is hidden from people.

questions.question: You have a test tomorrow. What goes with asking Allah for help?
questions.explanation: The Prophet taught people to seek what benefits them and ask Allah for help.

questions.question: You give to someone in need. Which intention is best?

options.text: To please Allah and help them

questions.explanation: Good deeds should be done with a sincere intention.

questions.question: You regret a sin. Which thought should guide you?

options.text: Allah's mercy can never reach me.
I should give up every good deed.
I can repent and seek Allah's mercy.

questions.explanation: Allah calls people not to despair of His mercy.

questions.question: You want to understand Allah's guidance. Which book should you learn from?
questions.explanation: The Quran is guidance from Allah.

questions.question: You want to learn how the Prophet prayed. Whose example should you follow?
questions.explanation: The Prophet taught Muslims to pray following his example.

questions.question: You enjoy a meal. What attitude fits belief in Allah's blessings?

options.text: Believing you will never need help

questions.explanation: Recognizing Allah's blessings should lead to gratitude.

questions.question: You have little money. Can you still call upon Allah?

options.text: Only if you can pay someone

questions.explanation: Allah's invitation to call upon Him is not limited to wealthy people.

questions.question: You have a difficult day. Which response fits faith?

options.text: Ask Allah for help and keep trying.
Stop caring about right and wrong.

questions.explanation: Seek Allah's help and do not give up on beneficial effort.

questions.question: A friend mentions Musa and Isa. How should you regard these prophets?
questions.explanation: Muslims believe in Allah's messengers, including Musa and Isa.

questions.question: You pray without anyone watching. Is public praise needed for Allah to know your worship?

options.text: Yes, you must post it online.
Yes, you must announce it first.

questions.explanation: Allah knows what is hidden as well as what is public.

questions.question: You realize you are doing something wrong. What is the right first response?

options.text: Keep doing it to avoid embarrassment.
Teach others to do it too.
Claim that wrong no longer matters.
Stop and turn back to Allah.

questions.explanation: Sincere repentance includes leaving the wrongdoing rather than knowingly persisting.

questions.question: You provide for your family sincerely for Allah. Can this be rewarded?
questions.explanation: Sincere spending on one's family can be an act of charity.

questions.question: You can do only a small good deed today. Does it still matter?

options.text: Only if it makes you famous
Yes, even a small good deed matters.
Only if it costs a lot

questions.explanation: The Quran teaches that even an atom's weight of good will be seen.

questions.question: You remember that you will answer to Allah. Which choice fits that belief?

options.text: Lie whenever no one can check.
Take what belongs to someone else.
Tell the truth even when a lie seems easier.
Hide every mistake by blaming others.

questions.explanation: Belief in accountability encourages responsible choices, and the Prophet praised truthfulness.

questions.question: You do not know the answer to a religious question. What should you do?

options.text: Say you do not know and ask someone knowledgeable.

questions.explanation: Asking knowledgeable people is better than pretending to know.
